findings.exact_text: Arda swung free on the cut length still gripped in his fist, and Nisa—reading the exact same moment he did—leaned back and hauled, and his hand found her wrist
findings.reason: He cut the line he was hanging from, yet holds the cut length and reaches her wrist across a falling gap. Mechanics are unclear and implausible.

findings.exact_text: There was no time to unlash.
findings.reason: Cutting the line he is hanging from dropped him, so the sacrifice is not needed to free himself and is counterproductive; the logic of the cut is muddled.

findings.exact_text: The glider still held where the old knot-trunk leaned.
findings.reason: The glider was steadied by the line, which Arda removed, and Nisa's glider is never accounted for; the glider holding without the line is unexplained.

findings.exact_text: the proof was lashed to his harness
findings.reason: The journal and tag were carried in hand or pack; lashing is never shown, and the tag is later taken out.

findings.exact_text: I want to see the corridor.
findings.reason: The corridor is below and behind the island, yet the ridge is treated as a vantage; also the bridge is crossed before the fork, and the return reaches the 'same' bridge ambiguously.

findings.exact_text: in the last light
findings.reason: The story ends in 'last light' and 'sunset' but morning storm clearing implied no time passage; also lantern lighting. Timing is loosely handled.

primary_audit.summary: Strong, mostly faithful story. Main issues are the muddled rope-cutting mechanics at the climax, some state details (glider, proof), a canon-adjacent age assertion, and a few awkward phrasings.

findings.exact_text: something she wished she didn't want
findings.reason: The nested “wished she didn't want” construction is strained and obscures whether she resents agreeing or resents wanting to agree.

findings.exact_text: dropped away to cloud sea
findings.reason: “Cloud sea” needs the article here; natural phrasing is “dropped away to the cloud sea.”

findings.exact_text: the same corridor we arrived
findings.reason: The relative construction is missing “through”: one arrives through a corridor, not simply “arrives a corridor.”

findings.exact_text: reading the exact same moment he did
findings.reason: One can read a situation or read a moment the same way, but “reading the exact same moment he did” is not idiomatic English.

secondary_audit.summary: The prose is highly fluent overall. Four sentences contain local naturalness defects involving a strained thought construction, a missing article, a missing preposition, and an unidiomatic action phrase.
